findings.reason: the plan tells authors a gate can be scoped to a section, exactly the guidance reckon-create gives to prefer gates over depends_on, and without the section-readiness wiring an author who does so gets the premature whole-plan blocking the skills steer them away from.
findings.text: readiness computes is_blocked from gate_blockers unconditionally, so gated_sections (parsed at _plan_html.py:618, stored at _store.py:2964, schema-validated at _schema.py:1092) changes only the graph edge, never the plan-level verdict the plan's §2 promises ("a failed gate therefore renders downstream sections and plans blocked"); the interface is wider than the behaviour it hides

findings.reason: the plan's own premise is one derivation with one owner ("state that can be computed must not also be stored"); it should name the roadmap blocker assembly (or a shared builder) as the owner both readers consume, or the two derivations keep drifting as measured.
findings.text: serve._derive_lifecycle assembles its own blocker list (unresolved_dependencies + sprint-item explicit + unpassed_gate_blockers) instead of consuming the assembly that owns it in roadmap.build_roadmap, and it has already drifted: roadmap's is_blocked carries held_blockers and plan_holding_decisions that serve's effective_status never sees, so the same plan can read blocked in one reader and open in the other

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the gate element grows a gated_sections surface (schema field, parser, edge logic) that its own plan-readiness consumer ignores, so an unpassed section-scoped gate blocks the whole plan regardless of the sections it names.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan routes gates "through the existing effective_status path" (singular) but no single owner assembles the blocking list; serve._derive_lifecycle re-lines the pieces and has already drifted from roadmap's assembly.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites and extends the existing machinery it depends on: gates mirror the decisions/followups element pattern, unpassed gates route through the existing effective_status/blocking derivation (reckon/lifecycle.py), staleness reuses doccheck's existing thresholds (reckon/doccheck.py), prose retirement extends the edit-transaction layer, and §2 explicitly declines to re-author the gate rule owned by uniform-worker-dispatch.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the gate element is explicitly justified as a layering over the established decisions/followups machinery and the existing blocking derivation rather than a parallel mechanism, and the one file it must share (SKILL.md) is fenced to its owner.
